classification.difficultyReason: Each dataset and the population statistic are explicitly identified. Students apply the taught calculator procedure, round to two decimal places, and directly interpret the lower SD as greater consistency; no choice of statistical method or reframing is needed.

content.prompt:
Maya and Jake each completed the same puzzle five times. Their times, in minutes, are listed below.
Maya: $12,\ 15,\ 16,\ 18,\ 19$
Jake: $10,\ 14,\ 17,\ 18,\ 21$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation of Maya's times. Round to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
Using 1-variable statistics, select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x&=2.449489\ldots\\\sigma_x&\approx2.45\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation of Jake's times. Round to 2 d.p.

answer.worked:
Using 1-variable statistics, select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x&=3.741657\ldots\\\sigma_x&\approx3.74\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Who had the more consistent times? Give a reason.

answer.short: Maya, because her lower standard deviation indicates less spread and more consistent times.
answer.worked: Maya's population standard deviation is lower: $2.45<3.74$. Her times have less spread, so they are more consistent.
